title: Devcontainer: pinned toolchain, agent hooks, and a workspace-scoped git wrapper
summary: This change turns the devcontainer image from a thin Rust box into the full factory runtime: it pins and checksum-verifies every tool (moon, gh, actionlint, uv, Node, pnpm, Bun, the four coding agents, dsh, SkillSpector/SkillEvaluator, archify skills), builds the dsh/omp/opencode integrations from the repo's own pnpm lockfile, installs each agent's hook wiring root-owned and read-only, and replaces the system-wide core.hooksPath with a git wrapper that forces /opt/factory/githooks only for repositories under the workspace mount. A new GitHub Actions workflow builds the image, and a suite of build-time shell tests proves the wrapper's refusals, the hook wiring, the read-only toolchain, and that no root cache or session state leaks into a layer.

nodes.label: Developer
nodes.summary: Runs the container, supplies GH_TOKEN, and drives the coding agents.

nodes.label: devcontainer.json
nodes.subtitle: workspaceMount + remoteEnv
nodes.summary: Now pins the bind mount to /workspace, forwards GH_TOKEN from the local environment, and its postCreateCommand checks osf, moon, node and pnpm versions.

nodes.label: Dockerfile
nodes.subtitle: +493 lines
nodes.summary: The single build recipe. Every downloaded tool is pinned by version and verified against a published SHA-256 before install; every installed tree is chowned to root and stripped of group/other write bits.

nodes.label: Pinned toolchain
nodes.subtitle: moon, gh, actionlint, uv, node, pnpm, bun
nodes.summary: moon, GitHub CLI, actionlint, uv, Node 22, pnpm via corepack, and Bun, each fetched from its own release tarball and checksum-verified.

nodes.label: Coding agents
nodes.subtitle: codex, claude-code, opencode, omp
nodes.summary: The four supported agents, installed as global npm packages into the root-owned Node install, then chmod go-w.

nodes.label: SkillSpector / SkillEvaluator
nodes.subtitle: uv tool install at pinned commits
nodes.summary: Installed from NVIDIA git history at full 40-character commits, with UV_TOOL_DIR and UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR moved out from under root's home so dev can read and execute them.

nodes.label: dsh
nodes.subtitle: @deepseek-ai/dsh 0.2.0-rc.2
nodes.summary: Installed from its own lockfile under /opt/dsh and symlinked onto PATH, so its dependency tree is reproducible independently of the repo's pnpm workspace.

nodes.label: Integration build
nodes.subtitle: pnpm --filter dsh,omp,opencode
nodes.summary: Builds the three writing-check integrations from the repo's own pnpm lockfile in a directory outside /workspace, so their dist/ output matches what CI already tests.

nodes.label: osf
nodes.subtitle: /opt/factory/bin/osf, mode 0555
nodes.summary: Built from the workspace crates with cargo cache mounts, installed root-owned and read-only.

nodes.label: Agent hook wiring
nodes.subtitle: codex /etc, claude + opencode system copies
nodes.summary: Each agent's hook file is written root-owned and read-only, with system-level copies for codex, claude-code and opencode so a changed HOME cannot move them; omp and dsh keep home-only copies.

nodes.label: dsh profiles
nodes.subtitle: factory + headless
nodes.summary: Both dsh profiles get the osf-dsh-plugin under node_modules and a cordis.patch.yml, locked root-owned and read-only except the cordis.yml dsh rewrites on every start.

nodes.label: Git hooks
nodes.subtitle: pre-commit, commit-msg, pre-push
nodes.summary: The three root-owned hook scripts that call osf; unchanged in content, but now reached through the wrapper's forced hooks path rather than a system-wide config.

nodes.label: git wrapper
nodes.subtitle: /opt/factory/bin/git
nodes.summary: Refuses --no-verify and -n on commit and --no-verify on push, then forces core.hooksPath=/opt/factory/githooks on the command line for repositories under OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT, and calls the real git.

nodes.label: real git
nodes.summary: The system git the wrapper execs once its checks pass.

nodes.label: osf hook
nodes.subtitle: stop and prompt events
nodes.summary: The hook entry point every agent's hook file calls; repository.rs changed to resolve the workspace root the same way the wrapper does.

nodes.label: Coding agent
nodes.subtitle: codex / claude / opencode / omp / dsh
nodes.summary: Whichever agent the developer runs; it fires its configured hook on prompt submit and turn end.

nodes.label: /workspace
nodes.subtitle: bind mount of the repo
nodes.summary: The one folder the wrapper treats as the workspace; devcontainer.json binds the repository here and OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT names the same value.

nodes.label: Build-time tests
nodes.subtitle: 9 shell scripts
nodes.summary: git-wrapper, git-hooks, agent-hooks, dsh-starts, coding-agent-tools, builder-tools, skills-installed, toolchain-readonly and image-clean all run during the build, so a broken wrapper or a leaked root cache fails the image instead of shipping.

nodes.label: devcontainer-image workflow
nodes.subtitle: .github/workflows/devcontainer-image.yml
nodes.summary: Builds the devcontainer image in CI, so the Dockerfile's own build-time tests run on every change to it.

edges.label: bind mount
edges.summary: workspaceMount and workspaceFolder now name /workspace explicitly, which is the value OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT carries into the wrapper.

edges.label: GH_TOKEN
edges.summary: remoteEnv forwards the host's GH_TOKEN into the container so gh and the builder role can open pull requests.
Each tool is fetched, checksum-verified and installed root-owned.

edges.label: core.hooksPath
edges.summary: The wrapper passes -c core.hooksPath=/opt/factory/githooks on the command line for repositories under the workspace, replacing the removed system-wide setting.

edges.label: prompt / stop
edges.summary: Each agent's hook file invokes osf hook for the one or two events osf supports.
repository.rs now resolves the workspace root consistently with the wrapper's OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT.

flows.title: A coding agent's prompt hook reaches osf
flows.summary: What happens between a developer submitting a prompt and osf hook answering: the agent reads its root-owned hook file, runs osf hook prompt, and osf resolves the workspace the same way the git wrapper does.

messages.label: read hook config
messages.note: Root-owned and read-only, so the agent cannot rewrite its own hook.

flows.title: A commit goes through the wrapper and the forced hooks
flows.summary: The path a git commit takes once the wrapper is on PATH: the wrapper rejects --no-verify and -n, forces the hooks path for repositories under the workspace, and only then execs the real git, which runs the root-owned pre-commit and commit-msg hooks.

messages.label: reject --no-verify / -n
messages.note: Refusal happens before the real git is ever reached.

messages.label: -c core.hooksPath=/opt/factory/githooks
messages.note: Only applied when the repository sits under OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT, so a scratch repo under /tmp is left alone.

views.title: Devcontainer image and runtime
views.summary: The image bakes a root-owned, checksum-verified toolchain and every agent's hook wiring; the runtime is the git wrapper, osf, and whichever agent the developer runs.

children.title: Hook wiring and the git wrapper
children.summary: How each agent's hook file and the git wrapper reach osf, and why the wrapper forces the hooks path instead of a system-wide config.

views.title: Prompt hook flow
views.summary: A developer's prompt reaches osf hook through the agent's root-owned hook file.

views.title: Commit through the wrapper
views.summary: The wrapper's refusals and forced hooks path, then the real git running the root-owned hooks.

steps.heading: The image is the contract
steps.body: Every tool is pinned by version and SHA-256, installed root-owned, and stripped of write bits.

steps.heading: Hooks are wired, not configured
steps.body: Each agent's hook file is baked in read-only, with system copies where the agent supports one.

steps.heading: The wrapper replaces the system config
steps.body: core.hooksPath is forced per call, only for repositories under the workspace mount.

steps.heading: A prompt reaches osf
steps.body: The agent reads its hook file and runs osf hook prompt, which resolves the same workspace root.

steps.heading: A commit cannot skip the hooks
steps.body: The wrapper refuses --no-verify and -n, then forces the hooks path before execing git.

steps.heading: The build proves itself
steps.body: Nine shell tests run during the build, so a broken wrapper or a leaked root cache fails the image.
